Our research targets this specific issue and proposes a novel approach to significantly decrease the number of samples requiring annotation by leveraging existing, sparse human annotations in conjunction with uncertainty-driven learning techniques. By combining costliest human labeling with cheaper automated labeling via pre-trained image and text models in a iterative framework that concentrates on minimally annotated samples with the highest prediction uncertainties, we successfully achieve near-perfect extraction F1-scores of over 95% on complex, visually rich layouts, with a data labeling cost of only 5% of conventional methods.

The interplay between magnetic order and spin-based phenomena within ferromagnetic semiconductors like EuS holds significant potential yet poses substantial challenges. Through the creation of heterostructures with metallic 2D materials such as InAs, the magnetoelectric effects can be readily manipulated. InAs was employed as a tunnel barrier or conductive layer in EuS-based structures, with the bonding interface's electronic properties examined using magnetic InAs EuS InAs sandwiches. The results reveal that the magnetoelectric response is influenced by the bonding arrangement of the EuS/InAs interface, with electronic transport monitoring and first-principles calculations both revealing a shift in chemical potential and shift in band offset resulting in an energy barrier for InAs. The findings also indicate that the In/As ratio is crucial in achieving optimal performance, with magnetic InAs EuS InAs structures exhibiting an energy barrier as low as 0.1 eV.

A significant result by Wadge can be clearer understood through the lens of effective descriptive set theory's understanding of Borel Wadge classes, particularly the effective Lusin separation theorem. Building on this background, our primary contribution lies in advancing the current limit of research on the effective categorization of Borel Wadge classes, achieved by introducing a precise definition of effective Wadge degree comparability. Our research demonstrates that any partition of the Baire space into Borel sets involves sets belonging to a finite number of distinct categories under this new definition. Furthermore, we show that any separation of Borel sets involves sets with a limited number of distinct categories, specifically not exceeding three. These results yield new insights into effective Cech complexity and effective perfect set property.

Highly parameterized deep neural network (DNN) models have transformed many critical applications, but their enormous size often poses challenges for deployment on resource-constrained devices. The resulting training inefficiencies can be costly, particularly when training large models like BERT takes an extended period. Recent advances in model pruning have enabled the creation of compact models, yet integrating them into the DNN training pipeline remains a complex task. The existing solutions are either cumbersome to implement or fail to deliver superior performance compared to their unpruned counterparts. In response to these challenges, we have developed ClickTrain, a cutting-edge model pruning framework that allows for seamless integration of structure-preserving pruning into DNN training for enhanced efficiency and accuracy. ClickTrain's innovative approach facilitates precise gradient propagation and parallel updates of the network structure, resulting in superior performance. The framework has been successfully tested on various fundamental and advanced training operators for foundational and attention-based networks, showcasing its remarkable ability to achieve significant model compression while maintaining high model accuracy and training speed. ClickTrain outperforms state-of-the-art models by achieving a 4.5× improvement in acceleration and 3.1× improvement in compression without compromising model accuracy. Additionally, the framework has demonstrated exceptional performance on multiple image classification and natural language inference datasets, out achieving notable gains in efficiency and accuracy.

We examine how modal operators in the non-commutative Lambek calculus enhance reasoning capabilities and whether they enable decision-making procedures to be determined. By integrating S4 axioms and functional interpretation of these operators into the distributive complete Lambek calculus, we achieved proof that reasoning remains complete with this addition; in contrast, complete reasoning was not achievable without a specific emphasis on associativity. Building on this proof, we developed a new system of natural deduction that improves time complexity from exponential to quadratic.

The observation of gravitational waves produced by neutron star-black hole collisions offers a distinct opportunity to explore the gravitational consequences of these events. Due to gravitational wave ambiguity, accurately distinguishing neutron stars from black holes remains a significant challenge when analyzing data detected by LIGO or Virgo. The uniqueness of NWBC signals in comparison to binary neutron star mergers presents an issue, as existing models may not adequately capture the complexity of these events. The proposed solution involves utilizing deep learning to analyze GW data, leveraging a convolutional neural network to differentiate NSBH signals from pure noise. The developed model demonstrates improved accuracy in classifying signals, surpassing traditional statistical methods with notable success rates. The success of this approach has significant implications for understanding the gravitational characteristics of these events.

Our study focuses on a newly identified exoplanet, TOI-5542 b, which is an extensive investigation of the system's characteristics and its verification through multiple observational approaches and advanced simulations. Utilizing precise radial velocity measurements, our analysis confirms the existence of TOI-5542 b, a Jupiter-like gas giant with a mass of $1.71^{+0.27}_{-0.24}$ $M_{\rm J}$, that completes its orbit around its host star every 3.7001029 $\pm$ 0.0003211 days. Studies combining Gaussian process and Markov chain Monte Carlo analyses reveal the system's semi-major axis to be $0.04775 \pm 0.00024$ AU, with a moderate eccentricity of $0.143 \pm 0.023$. Utilizing atmospheric modeling and Bayesian model comparison, we determine the star's age to lie between 1.16 and $6.28$ billion years, which places the system within the realm of old solar-type stars similar to HD82943. TOI-5542 b exhibits characteristics similar to other massive planets with substantial masses, high temperatures, highly eccentric orbits, and stars with metal-poor compositions, potentially indicating hot migration or high-eccentricity migration as the primary mechanism for its formation

This paper introduces an algorithm based on primal-dual smoothing to resolve discrete-time stochastic models known as Markov choice procedures, which involve minimizing cost under constraints related to expected values of Markov chain states. A tailored condition, the relative variable support condition, is introduced to ensure effective acceleration of the algorithm. Given its computational simplicity, the method proves suitable for implementation without extensive computational resources. Under this assumption, the method demonstrates a finite convergence rate to within any specified tolerance level, and more notably, its per-iteration time complexity is linear, thereby making it highly efficient. This efficiency is underscored by notable applications, such as those in risk-sensitive stochastic control and Black-Litterman strategy analysis, which benefit from the method's capabilities.

Mathematical expression recognition is a crucial application for human-computer interaction.
Current research focuses on online handwritten mathematical notation recognition.
However, offline recognition remains underexplored due to the unavailability of large annotated datasets.
In this study, we create a substantial dataset called CROH25-GMS, which integrates handwriting annotation files.
By utilizing the newly created dataset, we establish the dielectric constant of the material.
The results indicate that deep convolutional neural networks outperform recurrent neural networks in accuracy.

We explore sheaf cohomology from the perspective of supersymmetric quantum mechanics, using a line bundle with connection on a manifold. The supercharges in this framework lead to three key observations: first, the A-Dolbeault complex is seen as a supersymmetric theory with non-zero cohomology solely in odd degrees; second, an inequality arises from the positivity of the Hamiltonian Hamiltonian, relating the dimensions of cohomology groups to positive integers; third, an expansion of cohomology groups is achieved through the application of super Symplectic reduction and momentum map.

To examine the characteristics of variability in interaction processes within network systems, we initially employ a simple model representing a firefly synchronization mechanism to generate random networks with diverse topology variations. By analyzing these networks using quantitative metrics, we observe that their structure can be categorized into distinct and distinctively variable time scales. Subsequently, we develop a general model for the diffusion of correlated fluctuations on these networks and demonstrate that their dynamics can be unified under a two-scale framework. Leveraging this classification and the established model, we create an interaction process description based on probability distributions that are driven by the network structure's variability. This probable description is then applied to more intricate network models to validate its applicability in diverse system interactions.

Policy Gradient Reinforcement Learning algorithms often suffer from unreliable step sizes, which can be mitigated by leveraging time-reversible techniques, such as adding an Euler-Feynman operator to the policy update, to derive a more robust Hamiltonian Monte Carlo-based Reinforcement Learning method. This approach leverages asset pricing theory to model the Hamiltonian, which in turn provides more reliable trajectory evaluations. Moreover, it offers a more precise way to traverse the policy space by utilizing the symplectic nature of Hamiltonian dynamics, which conserves energy and ensures long-term stability. Experimental evaluations on classic control tasks demonstrate the superior performance of the new method, which achieves higher optimal rewards and variation reduction compared to traditional Trust Region methods.

This introductory proof of the Twin Prime Hypothesis relies on straightforward mathematical concepts such as divisibility, relatively prime properties, and prime-related functions, making it accessible to individuals with basic mathematical knowledge. The proof employs an introductory approach using infinite relatively prime sequences to analyze prime distribution patterns through polynomial expressions and offers two approaches to address Bachmann-Landau asymptotics, ultimately incorporating the use of the circle method to complete the proof.

The Real-time Navigation Manager (RTNM) implements a layered architecture that utilizes data from various sonar sensors to guide a mobile robot. Despite enabling successful long-term navigation, RTNM fails to effectively handle frequent near-field collisions due to its inability to give priority to up-to-date sonar data over outdated information. In response, we developed Sonar Blending, an sonar data integration technique inspired by back-end blending methods like Visual SLAM. Instant Sonar Blending operates on sonar data in real-time, improving the navigation performance for robots employing similar sensor setups. Our methodology demonstrated the ability to restrict the robot's movement away from obstacles within a specific sensor range and successfully handled noisy or missing sonar data without affecting the robot's long-term navigation capabilities. In addition to algorithmic adjustments, we modified the RTNM to incorporate our Sonar Blending approach and evaluated its efficacy using real-world test datasets. Our results show significant improvements in the robot's ability to navigate in real-time, specifically limiting the navigation error to under 17cm compared to under 30cm achieved by RTNM alone.

Nereid, one of Saturn's distant moons, exhibits an irregular orbit resulting from its varying distance from the Sun. Located in the outer regions of the solar system, Nereid is composed primarily of water ice and organic materials. Its reflective spectra were analyzed using the Nereid-CH4 filter, and spectral features in the near-infrared range were identified to understand its surface composition. Data on Nereid's albedo, red spectral slope, and crystalline water ice features were albedo-corrected to account for variations in albedo, revealing a diverse range of water ice and THOLIN material ratios on its surface. Red slopes on Nereid's surface suggest the presence of amorphous ice, while water ice features indicate temperatures below 40-50 Kelvin on Nereid's surface, likely due to its low albedo and distant orbit from the Sun.

This research provides a detailed examination of points and curves on certain types of surfaces defined over special sets of linear equations governed by specific types of triangular matrices. We calculate key characteristics such as dimensions and singular points on these surfaces using relationships between relationships between ideals in these matrices' containing rings. Dimensionless and projective surfaces are analyzed although some of their properties can be traced back to the original flat surfaces. Our analysis includes configurations of singular points and curves such as free lines on these surfaces defined in vector configurations and projective spaces respectively.

We employ model theory to analyze specific aspects of Pawlikowski's theorems regarding Tukey-order. In our approach, we prove that $ \mathcal{P}(\omega)/{\text{fin}} $ is minimal among minimal Tukey-orderings. Additionally, we obtain a relative version of Pawlikowski's theorems using tuple-sequences and use this to prove that there are no infinite descending or ascending chains in Tukey-order. These findings serve as model-theoretic proofs, bypassing traditional combinatorial methods.

Building upon the foundational Bayesian learning approach outlined in Papadopoulos et al. (2007), this paper proposes an advanced pessimism criterion for use in dynamic treatment strategies. The new criterion enables the use of Bayesian learning algorithms even when the underlying model parameters are only partially known. It achieves this by allowing the application of these algorithms in complex settings, including those with multiple interventions and dependent interventions. By allowing for the use of Bayesian algorithms under such conditions, this new pessimism criterion expands the scope of applications for value iteration and dynamic treatment strategies. It is demonstrated through empirical studies that the new pessimism criterion maintains the safety guarantees of dynamic treatment strategies while also resulting in higher average causal effects.

This abstract details our approach to dualities and applications of homological invariants for representations of quivers with orientation-less relationships, aiming to preserve invariance throughout dualization processes. A key technique employed involves utilizing invariants from homological theory, particularly Euler characteristics, to interpret dualities as equivalences between categories, specifically equivalences between homological categories, as seen in the dualities of self-injective algebras. We will examine two types of homological invariants: the characteristic polynomial invariants developed by Ringel and the Dao-Happel-Keeler invariant, showcasing their effectiveness through examples of super quivers, including those in mathematical physics contexts.

We employ the complexification of the $E_8$ lattice, specifically using Heisenberg group unitary irreducible representations, to model a system of qubits. The choice of lattice over qubits hinges on the desire for enhanced long-range interactions to support quantum entanglement and contextuality. We demonstrate that using $E_8$ yields increased correlations compared to using 15 binary qubits. Furthermore, we show that complexifying the $E_8$ root lattice leads to contextuality in the measurement of observables. Our analysis reveals that using the lattice of the complexified $E_8$ root system allows for greater entanglement and contextuality than its real-valued counterpart.

Within the flat bands of certain twisted bilayer graphene systems, we hypothesize a form of superconductivity driven by multiple bodily interactions. The dimensionality of this multiple-bodily superconductivity is established by a body-ordered vector representation of the superconducting gap, exhibiting vector symmetry under rotations within the confluence symmetry group. Furthermore, the gap parameter can be expressed through a vector potential linked to the topological properties of the occupied states below the gap. This results in the occurrence of a topological superconducting phase transition when the gap closes. The effective interaction governing this phenomenon is a form that is fifth-order in the electron field operators and is therefore robust against fluctuations near the critical point. The predictions outlined in this work may be verified through experiments using techniques such as angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and through manipulations enabled by Floquet engineering or the introduction of vacancies via ion irradiation, enabling the investigation of multiple-bodily superconductivity and topological properties in twisted bilayer graphene and similar materials.

We investigate and demonstrate the correctness of a generalized version of the linked groups theorem, which applies to locally compact, Abelian groups with at most countable generators and contains a closed, properly embedded subgroup with co-dimension 1.

Presence-absence data collection has become increasingly common across various fields such as biology and geography, resulting in massive datasets requiring analysis. Cluster analysis offers valuable insights, helping to uncover patterns and understand data characteristics. This study focuses on evaluating the performance of multiple clustering methods tailored to handling large volumes of binary data across diverse applications. To achieve this, we conducted thorough simulations based on diverse datasets and reviewed existing evaluation metrics. By examining how different methods behave under various conditions using both quantitative and qualitative approaches, our results show that choice of method significantly impacts outcomes across diverse datasets. Ultimately, our findings suggest that utilizing dynamic kernel clustering in combination with optimized feature selection effectively addresses real-world challenges associated with high-dimensional binary data in various fields.

In recent years, working with RGB-SAO and RGB-D-SAO sensing systems has become increasingly popular. Existing methods for salient object detection are tailored to specific systems, limiting their adaptability to different sensing models. This research introduces an integrated approach that allows salient object detection using both RGB and RGB-D images. The proposed method leverages a novel representation that combines features from RGB and additional color or depth information, if available. The proposed framework's efficacy is demonstrated through comprehensive evaluations on a suite of public datasets. The results indicate that the integrated method outperforms other models in various configurations when processing RGB and RGB-D images.

The UM-IU@LING system participated in the SemEval-2019 work on identifying aggression in social media posts, focusing on determining whether a tweet is aggressively directed at the author or another user. The challenge involved four sub-tasks: detecting overt aggression, subtle aggression, no aggression, and aggression towards self or others. The team achieved state-of-the-art results on two of these tasks through a combination of fast feature extraction, training a support vector machine, and fine-tuning BERT on the dataset for fine-tuned performance.

This paper examines the fractional parts that result from dividing symmetrical numbers by powers of ten. It also determines equivalent results for all numbers and explores how these quotients relate one another. Similar analysis is conducted using antisymmetrical numbers. By examining the quotients of both categories, whole number and remainder values can be obtained. Ultimately, numbers can be isolated based on their remainders. These methods provide numbers with unique properties and expanded application possibilities.

Computed tomography (CT) uses X-ray projections to reconstruct cross-sectional images of internal structures within an object. As objects grow in size, ensuring accurate, high-quality imaging becomes increasingly difficult due to material variations that can impede image formation. These variations can be particularly problematic in medical settings, where examining varying tissue types demands imaging at multiple energy levels. Current techniques struggle due to a lack of advanced material modeling and limited data due to scanning constraints. To overcome these challenges, our study presents a novel variational reconstruction method that combines accurate polyenergetic modeling, noise reduction, and material decomposition. Through simulation tests on realistic data, we demonstrate that our approach surpasses conventional non-iterative and variational methods in both quantitative and qualitative assessments.

Recent advancements in handwritten text recognition have heavily relied on deep learning-based approaches that require substantial, carefully prepared training datasets, particularly those that incorporate varied character compositions. To circumvent this constraint, we propose a novel strategy to create representative training data from a minimal collection of handwritten samples. Our approach leverages low-resource data to generate synthetic character variations, incorporating optical transformations and character merging based on resource scarcity. Moreover, we introduce a specialized evaluation metric to assess the efficacy of our data augmentation technique by analyzing the progress of a baseline model using both genuine and modified training data. Through extensive testing on a robust handwritten text recognition model, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in optimizing performance with a minimized amount of annotated training data.

Utilizing ab initio methods to study nuclear properties has seen new avenues opened up, thanks in part to advances in computational techniques and the development of personalized interaction operators derived from precise, measured nuclear data. This paper demonstrates the feasibility of extensive calculations even when working with very complex nuclei, specifically those weighing 193 and 194, by employing the ab initio no-core shell model. These computed results for the specific pattern of nuclear shell occupancy are then compared to direct experimental data obtained through the use of laser spectroscopy. The computed patterns are found to be in close correspondence with the experimental findings, specifically showing the presence of two distinct, low-energy long-range nuclear vibrations. Furthermore, the calculated energy requirements for adding individual neutrons to lighter, odd-neutron nuclei, ranging from 179 to 181, are also determined and found to closely match the measured data obtained through direct experiment.

Quantum systems exhibiting topological properties showcase unique characteristics distinct from conventional ones. Firstly, the descriptions of these models rely heavily on discussions about singularities and characteristics that arise from long-range connections. Secondly, the topological properties provide protection against disturbances due to their nature, resulting in exceptional applications for quantum information processing. Due to their complexity, the descriptions of these models often rely on advanced and abstract concepts, posing difficulties for students to grasp using traditional methods. However, utilizing numerical simulations enables students to explore the characteristics of these models and perform experiments similar to those possible in the realm of classical physics. This tutorial begins by introducing essential descriptions for one-dimensional models, the SSH model being one such example, and offers various approaches for calculating topological properties along with one method to compute the wave functions exactly using linear algebra techniques. The SSH model exhibits exceptional nondegenerate edge states that provide protection against disturbances, which the tutorial examines by simulating the effects of disturbances and comparing them to conventional models. The analysis of this model also includes discussions about topological occurrence wave functions and quantum entanglement and their descriptions by spectral dimensions and mutual information.

This study determines the exact conditions under which composition operators are both bounded and compact in certain weighted Bergman spaces associated with a wider class of convex domains in the plane. Furthermore, it generalizes existing findings for specific types of unbounded domains and explores the composition operator properties in Bergman spaces linked with domains having analytic boundaries.

We investigate two-loop dual supergravity in the AdS$_5\times$S$^5$ spacetime using field theory methods. The data for this analysis is obtained from the stress-energy tensor's two-loop correlation functions in N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory, specifically its spherical, non-protected components with spin-2 and spin-4. By employing multiloop conformal block decomposition, we isolate these components and determine their coefficients with the aid of multipoint constraints from the conformal bootstrap method. The resulting expansion of these components allows us to directly compare with multiloop integrability data in the AdS/CFT correspondence, thereby obtaining precise values for some previously unknown graviton coupling constants in dual supergravity.

In high-performance computing environments, particularly when executing large-scale simulations on GPUs, developers often face limitations due to the restrictive capabilities of existing memory allocators. These memory allocators typically cause inefficient memory access and substantial memory usage due to the addition of indexing data and redundant memory blocks. To address this issue, we introduce DynaSOAr, an innovative dynamic memory allocator specifically designed for Object-oriented development on GPUs. DynaSOAr leverages the inherent object structure to optimize memory allocation by attaching indexing data directly to each object, and employs concurrent access to unused memory blocks for efficient allocation. Through our experimental analysis, DynaSOAr demonstrates improved performance, reduced memory usage, and better scalability, making it an ideal memory allocator for GPU-based object-oriented development.

This study explores minimal U(1)_X standard models derived from a U(1)_X extension of the Standard Model, which is based on an SO(10) group and includes right-handed neutrinos. These models are examined in the context of low-energy experiments, with a particular focus on the muon anomalous magnetic moment, neutrino oscillations, and electric dipole moments of fermions, as well as couplings to Z bosons. It is discovered that flavor physics can be largely characterized by two parameters within this research. However, further analysis of the muon anomalous magnetic moment reveals that additional right-handed neutrinos are required to achieve the observed anomalous magnetism for specific choices of flavor parameters, contradicting the original assumptions from SO(10). Z boson couplings were analyzed using LHC data and it is determined that Z → μμ has distinct predictions compared to other Z penguin searches, resulting in significant restrictions on the model parameters, with further implications for neutrino oscillations.

Plants exert pressure by filling their straw conduits with liquid under positive tension, 
which compensates for negative mechanical stress using the conduit's positive pressure, 
thus contributing to the plant's structural integrity. This phenomenon was utilized by 
Darwin in his exploration of stress and strain on straw ends under pressure. The current study 
presents the derivation of longitudinal stress in a straw conduit filled with liquid under tension 
considering Poisson effects via Mohr's theory of stress analysis. The effect of Poisson remains 
insignificant due to the dominance of longitudinal stress over transverse stress. The study 
utilizes stress-strain relationships and the linear theory of elasticity to calculate the strain 
on the straw wall, which, in turn, affects the liquid's volume change via the liquid's bulk modulus. 
The findings demonstrate that the strain on the straw wall leads to negative mechanical stress 
within the straw, counteracting the liquid's tensile pressure and enhancing the plant's structural 
integrity. The study refers to the work published in Biomechanics and cell physiology in 2021.

Recent developments in machine learning have introduced novel methods to manage uncertainty, but their integration into Bayesian models remains a significant challenge. We have developed a conservative approach rooted in credal analysis that allows us to assess the reliability of probabilistic models with imprecise uncertainty representations, using probabilistic logic constraints. By framing our method as an optimization problem on a widely-used inference engine, we can efficiently handle large models through the exploitation of probabilistic circuit structures. The result is a significant reduction in computational requirements without sacrificing accuracy. The method's performance was validated through comparisons with traditional Bayesian approaches and demonstrated its applicability on models containing latent variables defined by Markov random fields.

We examine the behavior of accelerated impurities within superfluids modeled as superfluid Bosons and Fermi liquids, respectively, focusing on scenarios involving large accelerations. Within the superfluid model, we demonstrate that the impurity exhibits Bloch oscillations characterized by periodic periods and amplitudes that depend on the superfluid's density. In contrast, the Fermi liquid model exhibits continuous growth in both the oscillation period and amplitude. Notably, we develop a new approach utilizing current operator dynamics to predict the oscillation periods and amplitudes, which aligns with the predictions from the Kubo formula and many-body perturbation theory. Our analysis also reveals that the growth rate of the oscillation period and amplitude in the Fermi liquid is linked to the presence of vortices within Vland's fermion model.

A code that possesses neighbour-transitivity is defined by a property where all codewords with non-zero weight have the same pattern of distances to other non-zero codewords. Researchers have previously explored neighbour-transitive codes in various types of geometries, including generalised quadrangles, and given specific minimum partial dispersion values for codes with particular lengths and sizes. This research identifies a class of neighbour-transitive codes in various generalised quadrangles, leading to improved lower bounds for partial dispersions in these codes. Furthermore, a classification of neighbour-transitive binary codes in thick generalised quadrangles has been established.

Investigating the spatial distribution of mass within the CMZ is crucial for understanding its complex astrophysics. Current research relies on 3D mass models, but these are often accompanied by large uncertainties. A more accurate approach would involve analyzing 2D projections of CMZ clumps. We propose a new method to quantify mass distributions by calculating the 2D correlation function from gamma-ray burst positions, comparing its results to those from a uniform sky distribution and assuming an isotropic 3D mass distribution, thereby allowing us to infer mass surface density maps in the CMZ. Our analysis reveals a significant concentration of mass towards the Galactic plane and identifies a notable rim-like structure at a distance of approximately 100 pc from the galactic plane, mass densities in the CMZ are significantly higher than those in the surrounding long bar structure, with values reaching up to 10^4 M_sun/pc^2. Our findings suggest the CMZ exhibits substantial mass irregularities on various spatial scales, with possible anisotropies in mass configurations量达10\% on scales of 100-200 pc.

After a sudden high-fluence x-ray absorption edge experiment, electrons and holes migrate and recombine in various ways, which significantly alters the absorption spectra. To better understand and analyze these spectra, we developed a comprehensive framework that accounts for these changes in real-time. This model takes into consideration both direct and indirect ionization caused by photon absorption and subsequent electron-hole pair generation, as well as the complex relaxation dynamics influenced by band structure and material properties. By applying this framework to the experimental data of LiNbO3, we found that our high-fluence population model accurately predicts the observed transient absorption spectra, outperforming previous low-fluence models and revealing a high pair recombination rate under extreme excitation conditions. This study showcases the model's potential to investigate the dynamic properties of materials under extreme conditions, enabling researchers to explore and map these rates and population states.

This project presents a ultra-low-power ultra-wide temperature range detector capable of withstanding temperatures from -40{\deg}C to 125{\deg}C, featuring an on-chip ultra-small thermal sensor. With enhancements to its architecture and transconductance amplifier, the detector achieves a resolution of 0.24{\deg}C, along with precise low and high temperature thresholds of 0.02 and 0.08 respectively. Furthermore, its fully differential architecture contributes to reduced inaccuracies amounting to 0.01 at the lowest temperature setting, resulting in an overall 16-bit accuracy. Furthermore, its fully differential architecture contributes to minimized inaccuracies amounting to 0.01 at the lowest temperature setting, contributing to an overall 16-bit accuracy. Utilizing a 130nm CMOS technology, experiments demonstrate an operational voltage range from 0.6V to 1.8V, combined with a supply current of 155{\mu}A, leading to energy consumption of 1.16uJ per conversion, along with energy efficiency of 1.06nJ per bit.

Quantum correlations play a pivotal role in the development of quantum information technology. The single qubit state's ability to create entanglement is limited due to its capacity to only control one degree of freedom. By leveraging quantum scissors technology, which enables the manipulation of both amplitude and phase through measurement and conditioning, we can create polarization entanglement without sacrificing capacity. The present research demonstrates the possibility of deterministically generating polarization entanglement on demand using quantum scissors, providing a crucial building block for the development of quantum information processing systems.

A set of vertices in a metric space forms a $t$-spanner when the distance between any pair is multiplied by at most $t$ and they are connected by edges in the metric space. This concept is relevant to various practical issues in computer networking and algorithm design, although finding the smallest possible Euclidean spanner with the fewest edges in various dimensions remains computationally difficult. Research has shown that very small Euclidean spanners in dimensions four and higher have a lower bound on the product of stretch and edge count that increases exponentially with dimension. To gain insight into this phenomenon, this study introduces a new concept: virtual Euclidean spanners, which are theoretical structures combining subsets of a point set with weights on complete subgraphs to approximate the original metric. A detailed analysis is provided to show the geometric and probabilistic properties of these spanners across different dimensions.

Accurate device identification in IoT networks is vital for ensuring secure and monitored connections. IoT components have varying capabilities, leading to differences in identification costs. This paper presents a innovative approach for device identification that considers energy costs, utilizing device capabilities to extract a subset of features for classification. The proposed method uses a hybrid algorithm that integrates KMeans clustering with Local Derivative Decision Rule guided filtering to select cost-efficient features. The effectiveness of this approach is evaluated through experiments on IoT device data, with results showing improved accuracy over existing methods and substantial exchange reductions in IoT networks.

Godel modal logic extends the strong Godel algebra by incorporating topological spaces with open neighborhoods defined by a modality. The class of all algebras that satisfy the logic's axioms, beyond semantic validity, is investigated in this research. We demonstrate that algebras with separable topological spaces are inherently fulfilling the logic's requirements. Building upon this finding, we define and examine expanded classes of relational structures through the introduction of multiple modalities and n-ary relations. We then construct specific relational structures that inherently satisfy the logic's axioms in ways that defy proof through syntactic methods. We also consider extensions of Godel modal logic that include strong completeness theorems for normal and separable Godel algebras with topological interpretations, as well as their variants incorporating n-ary relations.

This study explores utilizing external bilingual data sources for real-time word alignment between pairs of languages that lack training data. It investigates various sources, such as dictionaries and translators, along with different approaches like using them separately or in combination. The results demonstrate the efficacy of integrating multiple external data sources and provide insights into how they can be effectively utilized for word alignment purposes. The findings also offer a basis for further research and development in this area.

This research introduces an algorithm for creating a strategy profile that can serve as a Nash Equilibrium in a game with continuous variables and compact domains. The algorithm's output guarantees that no participant can significantly improve their payoff by unilaterally changing their strategy. We demonstrate the algorithm's ability to reach such a equilibrium within a SPOK time and show that it can still be applied in games where participants have convex preferences or belong to specific regular classes.

The theoretical framework of dark energy is proposed by Primordial Black Holes (PBHs), assuming that their mass corresponds to the current cosmic matter density.  In a Python code named PopSyCLE, a simulation models the evolution of a single PBH type from the radiation-dominated to the matter-dominated universe, determining the time necessary for their combined mass to equal current cosmic mass under the assumption of complete conversion.  Code has been developed to automate this simulation, reducing the need for manual adjustments.  However, simulating the full cosmic timeline may be unnecessary for masses of PBHs greater than 10^{-6} solar masses, as their evolution into the current epoch is largely predictable.  Employing PopSyCLE allows researchers to rapidly evaluate the feasibility of the PBH dark energy hypothesis for a wide range of PBH masses.  While simulating the full cosmic timeline is not needed, code adjustments may still be required when transitioning from one PBH model to another.  Using the established equation of state parameter, popsycle determines the PBH formation time based on a user-specified formation mass and a cosmological parameter that influences formation time based on the PBH mass, particularly for masses less than 10^{-6} solar masses where PBH formation occurs during the radiation-dominated universe.  For PBHs with masses greater than 10^{-6} solar masses where PBH formation occurs during the matter-dominated universe, adjusting the formation mass can alter the cosmic age at

We studied the cross-sectional shapes of cross-sections of stabilized stages formed by rigid wedges made of balls with varying radii and in different shape configurations including regular polygons, irregular polygons, and with both increasing and decreasing radii along the z-axis. The cross-section modulates with a splay and some shapes have additional twist or sags due to varying radii and constraints preventing relative rotation between neighboring balls. Despite these complexities, the modulations follow expectations based on energy minimization principles. Our investigation into these structures could provide valuable insights into understanding polydisperse liquid crystals and other self-assembling ball-like systems.

Studio Ghibli Films Inc. Studios in Tokyo released the documentary "The Girl and the Library" in 2022, depicting fictional characters created through a Markov Random Field (MRF) on the sphere S^2, where an initial creation involved manually designing three base filters, observed at lattice points, with projections from Gaussian 3D features onto the sphere S^2, noted for their artistic value and not intended to represent real-life locations. This work builds upon earlier research involving static Gaussian processes and develops recurrences for the Markov property on the sphere S^d by generalizing step creation from vertical to inclined planes in S^d+1 projective space, applying these concepts to characters originally established on S^2 and extended to the d-dimensional sphere S^d for any d >= 2. Additionally, we explore the effects of noise on these constructed models.

Traditional, engineering-based approaches to visualizing complex systems face fundamental limitations due to measurement-induced disturbance and data acquisition constraints. A novel approach based on single-pixel quantum visualization using undetected-pixel interference has shown promising results in characterizing complex systems with high fidelity without disruption. However, this method previously relied on entangled photons. This work presents an innovation in single-pixel quantum visualization by successfully utilizing both undetected and detection-free techniques with a source of photon pairs produced through spontaneous parametric down-conversion. Moreover, this achievement holds significant implications for quantum imaging quality enhancement and may lead to the development of quantum-enhanced imaging systems operating in the visible spectrum.

The behavior of dry foams can be effectively described using a model that incorporates a specific elastic description, provided the size of the bubbles remains significantly smaller than the size of the surface area. However, when the surface texture consists of features that are comparable in size to the bubble size, this conventional model fails to describe the friction experienced during sliding. To understand the observed friction in such cases, researchers conducted numerical simulations and found that the regular patterns within the foam structure play a crucial role in determining the friction coefficient. Moreover, certain aspects of the simulated foam's deformation exhibit characteristics that resemble those typically associated with semisolid materials.

This study presents an enhanced deep learning framework for accurately diagnosing skin cancers. Building on the existing transfer learning approach that utilized ImageNet pre-trained models, our method improves the learning process and detection rate of skin cancer classes by introducing a novel training strategy. The proposed technique incorporates data enhancement, a model regularization technique utilizing Shannon entropy, and a new training method that counts occurrences of each class to address data imbalance. The latter enables the identification of outlier samples that are excluded to improve overall performance. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach by achieving higher accuracy rates of 96.8%, 97.3%, and 97.5% in detecting the skin cancer classes of melanoma, benign, and BCC.

Researchers used advanced x-ray spectroscopy techniques to study the behavior of electrons in sodium over extremely short time frames. Their findings reveal that as energy varies, so does the probability of an excited quasi-particle undergoing interactions with other electrons. Notably, these interactions significantly influence how quickly quasi-particles lose their characteristics. In contrast to previously observed phenomena in other materials, the experiments showed that interactions among electrons dominate over another source of energy dissipation until a certain energy threshold is reached. This discovery underscores the importance of considering quantum effects that operate over extremely short time frames. Furthermore, the experiments provided measured values for how quickly quasi-particles survive within sodium, which can be compared to theoretical predictions based on basic quantum mechanical models. These models accurately replicate the observed energy-dependent changes in survival times but underestimate the actual duration by a factor of ten.

In nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, applying phase space methods to study systems with complex dynamics is hindered by a substantial variation in phase space volume during expansion. This application is crucial for utilizing nonequilibrium framework methods, such as the generalized nonequilibrium work theorem and the generalised nonequilibrium fluctuation dissipation theorem. This research demonstrates how to successfully apply these theorems to systems with complex dynamics and large scale transformations by utilizing paths generated by modified Hamiltonians. This approach preserves the phase space volume and enables nonequilibrium framework methods to be effectively used for nonequilibrium processes involving large scale transformations.

An explicit graph decomposition formula is established for the Kontsevich weights of links and curvatures graphs associated with any given symplectic Poisson structure. Furthermore, it's proven that the computed weights match the weights previously determined through the residue series method introduced by Bar-Natan, a finding that provides an explicit verification of the mechanical 5-term relation's validity. Building upon this evidence, the method's potential as a practical tool for computing links and curvature weights is demonstrated. Weight calculations for the trefoil knot are provided to illustrate this point. With the proposed formula, the mode of operation for these weights is shown to primarily involve determining the PBW expansion coefficients of a canonical Poisson structure as well as its corresponding weight.

We've investigated localised modes within woodpile and diatomic granular arrays in the seismically active frequency range, initially examining the role of nonlinearity. We found that the mode localisation effect, previously attributed to disorder, can occur due to a combination of low-level nonlinearity and disorder. As a result, the mode localisation is extensive, even in scenarios involving minimal nonlinelectricity and disorder. We further explored this phenomenon by conducting comprehensive numerical simulations and theoretical models, taking into consideration polymeric materials that can reduce both types of disorder. Our work has revealed new opportunities to control waves in such systems, leading to the development of nanoptera self-localised modes, which feature an oscillating peak that stabilises due to a balance between disorder-induced localisation and low-level nonlinearity.

Non-Gaussian patterns in cosmological signals may reveal signatures of heavy particles interacting with the inflaton. These interactions can occur directly through particle exchange between the inflaton and lighter fluctuations, resulting in non-Gaussian signals detectable through a "cosmological collider" effect. This phenomenon can also arise through indirect interactions via spiral-shaped features in the inflaton perturbations generated by features in multi-field inflation trajectories. These features, such as those in multi-field inflation, cause detectable imprints on the signals across various scales. We introduce the concept of primal features to describe any feature in the inflaton perturbations that can lead to heavy particle exchange signals within the non-Gaussian signals. We analyze the conditions under which primal features arise in scenarios including traditional multi-field inflation and heavy particle interactions through the breakdown of approximate symmetries.

We introduce a new class of graphs called accordion graphs and provide a method to determine all infinite families of cities in these graphs. We then explore the isomorphism between cities in these graphs and the graphs known as quartic circulants, using an algorithm that works for all cities in these graphs and has a time complexity of O(n^2).

We investigate two instances of three-state quantum walkers that asymptotically display similar behavior in evolution.  By leveraging the symmetry between the two models, we derive exact transition probabilities and dynamic correlations.  Our analysis confirms that the models exhibit dynamical scaling, characterized by universal distribution patterns.  Furthermore, we find that the distributions converge to the Airy function, which is typical of quantum harmonic oscillators near their equilibrium state.  This convergence occurs both centrally and when interacting with the boundaries of the grating.  Our results provide new insight and precision into the behavior of quantum walkers.

The self-supervised approach to learning vision representations via contrastive loss has achieved notable success with methods like contrastive predictive coding (CPC) and self-supervised signal learning (SSL). However, applying this loss directly to self-supervised learning with vision transformers (ViT) has been challenging, as our initial experiments revealed inconsistent performance and a narrow region of effective hyperparameters. In an attempt to overcome these obstacles, we explored characteristics of effective self-supervised learning extensions for ViT and discovered the benefits of incorporating inductive biases into the attention mechanism used in ViT. Specifically, our research focused on two extensions: limiting the look-ahead depth and restricting the look-around radius. Introducing these constraints has been found to enhance the self-supervised learning performance with ViT, enabling better generalization and more robust results. As a result, our self-supervised ViT model now surpasses the previous state-of-the-art models, particularly when using larger transformer sizes in comparison to earlier models based on smaller image sizes and smaller heads.

A combination integral-conformal age-density parameter has demonstrated considerable success in describing the universe's evolution during combined dark energy and dark matter phases. However, we discover that these dynamics are largely unaffected by assuming a dissipative process, which we attribute to the COE point exhibiting stability only when the combination parameter is extremely low or non-existent. Consequently, the dissipative mechanism's inclusion renders it redundant in dark energy dark matter models utilizing this combination parameter.

A simple, direct proof of a key theorem regarding incompressible Euler equations is presented here. This proof validates the loss of derivative phenomenon by demonstrating that in order for solutions to exist, the loss of derivative must occur in a quasinormed space where the loss of derivative occurs solely in a norm that loses more than one derivative in a Besov space is shown as a consequence of the proof. Furthermore, an example of a solution that exhibits the loss of the derivative in such a Besov space is also presented. Finally, a related finding from a prior paper by the author and T. Hmidi that relates to the inverse problem of deriving equations from data is discussed.

Generative diffusion models are renowned for their ability to generate high-quality synthetic data, but they often fall short when tasked with controlled data generation. Text-to-image diffusion models, in particular, struggle to create images based on complex, multifaceted text descriptions, resulting in unpredictable outcomes that may not adhere to the specified constraints. The issue stems from a lack of clear guidance on which semantic elements to prioritize during controlled data generation. This research aims to bridge this gap by developing the Steady Creator, a framework that enables stable and reliable data generation by harnessing the power of human expertise. The framework accomplishes this by extracting text-based semantic patterns, facilitating human assessment of their adherence to custom constraints, and incorporating these evaluations into a reinforcement learning process to realign the diffusion model's capabilities with desired data characteristics. Through the framework, we demonstrate improved data quality and enhanced compliance with customized constraints in the realm of outpainting and attribute manipulation tasks, showcasing more consistent performance and lower variance compared to existing diffusion models.

A new concealment technique based on Bayesian Neural Networks is presented, allowing the reversible embedding of $8$-bit sequences into image data. Initially, a network trained to predict pixel values in original images is created. An optimized version of this network is then generated, incorporating a reversible module that embeds residual information about the original pixel values, determined by comparing predicted and actual values. This embedded information enables an estimator to recover original pixel values at the decoder. The approach demonstrates strong concealment capabilities across various image formats, while achieving relatively low concealment rates, particularly when evaluating it against traditional methods such as ASK.

This study thoroughly investigates the possibility that $J/\psi$ decays into invisible particles. Such decays would directly relate to how neutrino masses and dark energy influence things. If $J/\psi$ decays into invisible particles, they would directly relate to how neutrino masses and dark energy influence things. If $J/\psi$ shows these invisible decays, an alternative to the $\Lambda$CDM model arises under conditions where new physics is driven by the same energy scale at which dark energy and potential neutrino masses occur. However, current data on dark energy acceleration suggests this energy scale is quite minuscule. Therefore, the invisible $J/\psi$ decays are highly unlikely based on present evidence. Additionally, we explore the conditions under which these invisible $J/\psi$ decays might become detectable in the near future.

Observations from the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope reveal the presence of bright features within the solar coronal plasma. Through the analysis of emission in the 1083 Å wavelength, the bright spots exhibit characteristics that suggest they consist of two distinct parts. By applying Bayesian methods, the distribution of these spots was mapped and the resulting data confirmed a two-part structure. The underlying differences can be attributed to variations in plasma density and temperature. The research indicates the presence of both cool cool-spot bright spots (around 5-15 eV) and hot hot-spot bright spots (around 20-30 eV). The frequency of the cool spots was found to be significantly higher, approximately ten times more prevalent than the hot spots. The cool spots are believed to be formed by small magnetic flux structures with lengths of a few hundred kilometers, arising from the solar photosphere. In contrast, the hot spots are thought to correspond to larger magnetic flux structures in the solar atmosphere, where the temperature is more likely to be around 20-30 eV.

In human perception, identifying moving objects in video can be significantly expedited even when only a minimal segment of the motion is available. This study examines whether the richness of information contained within these minimal motion segments is responsible for their efficacy. Using eye-tracking technology, the movement of human gaze has been found to guide identification processes towards object-relevant areas, such as a vehicle's headlights. Building on these insights, a model called Dynamic Identification Model (DIM) incorporates attention mechanisms to efficiently locate critical dynamic features within motion clips, minimizing redundancy in processing. When tested against a model without such attention-based optimization, DIM demonstrates improved identification accuracy with lower computational demands.

If cosmic magnetic fields existed before the Big Bang in a monopole-heavy environment, they could have been preserved throughout the universe's history, eliminating the need for their generation through dynamo mechanisms. Instead, they would have simply survived, implying a distinct origin story for these fields. This concept, known as the monopole shadow matter hypothesis, might explain various astrophysical phenomena, including the fields observed on the sun, Earth, and other galaxies, as well as ancient magnetic fields in the oldest rocks on Earth. Furthermore, this hypothesis could also account for the magnetic fields of the sun and Earth, which cycle in intensity rather than remaining static, as well as the magnetic fields of other celestial bodies such as other stars and planets. Essentially, this theory suggests that if these magnetic fields share a common, primordial origin, they would exhibit less variability than expected under dynamo-based generation models.

For the first time, this research explores using the Transformer model for climate predictions. However, due to its limitations in processing long sequences, it's impractical for climate modeling. This problem's solution could lie in using large batch sizes and leveraging GPUs' parallel processing capabilities. Nonetheless, this solution is largely unfeasible due to the substantial upfront costs and limited hardware availability. This paper presents a novel model, Weatherformer, designed specifically for climate prediction. It combines the SW-VAE architecture with a novel SWCA layer, enabling efficient processing of 3D climate sequences. By effectively capturing both spatial and temporal dependencies, Weatherformer outperforms competing models, including ESTR and TiGE, across multiple prediction scenarios and ultimately validates its effectiveness with real-world accuracy tests.

This study examines three-higgs-doublet models, featuring the $S_3$ symmetry, with an emphasis on their dark matter implications. A distinct characteristic of the models is the additional presence of CP-odd scalars. Within the $S_3$-invariant framework, dark matter candidates consist of either scalar or vector particles. We establish the conditions for dark matter stability and calculate their production rates during the early universe. We also consider various decay options of scalar particles and vector particles, as well as their associated bound state formations, prior to presenting our numerical results. We analyze both direct and indirect detection outcomes for dark matter vector particles and show that certain parameter regions remain viable under current experimental constraints.

A density matrix's positivity in a particular form does not guarantee its invertibility in bipartite systems, based on examples from q4 x q4 and q8 x q8 systems. On a bipartite system's Hilbert space, there exists a presumed existence of density matrices with both PPT and entanglement properties, known as PPT entangled density matrices, or PDEs, which are unique to bipartite systems. However, these matrices cannot be extended to non-separable partitions' tensor product systems in any way. The PPT quadrilateral hypothesis posits that such a quadrilateral cannot be formed by combining PPT matrices within both the Alice Bob and Alice Bob2 systems' spaces. We demonstrate through algebraic proof that both q2 x q4 and q4 x q8 systems violate this hypothesis, whereas the q3 x q3 system appears to comply with it.

Neuronal traffic jams can impede communication between neurons, potentially causing misfires and signaling disorders. To maintain homeostatic balance, neurons must adjust ion transport mechanisms to control intracellular concentrations. This study models this regulation process and the effects of congestion using an optimal control model for a system of partial differential equations with maximum flux constraints. Through analytical and numerical solutions, the model's unique equilibrium is examined under various levels of congestion, its stable properties confirmed, and results validated in multiple scenarios. Solutions are further computed in specific cases notable in literature. The model enables exploration of neurite congestion's impact on ion transport regulation and offers quantitative measures. By analyzing the model, we find that congestion can cause overregulation, leading to congested states. These findings on neurite congestion and ion transport regulation contribute to understanding neuron function and signaling difficulties.

Financial networks consist of numerous entities interacting through various transactions. From the perspective of graph theory, these interactions can be represented as a graph where different types of nodes and edges emerge. However, most financial networks are large and complex, often containing numerous types of nodes and edges that make pattern detection challenging. As a result, identifying patterns within these networks can be difficult, but finding meaningful patterns can provide valuable insights into their overall structure and behavior. In this research, we focus on novel pattern mining techniques for large financial networks with multiple entity types and edge directions. We introduce and adapt motif-based measures to analyze financial networks, providing the first comprehensive analysis of a large network, specifically Nemo, which links software development projects and individuals through transactional data. Our initial exploration of Nemo reveals its unique characteristics and highlights the value of network analysis in understanding and leveraging large financial networks for practical purposes.

As a star retreats from the innermost stable orbit around a black hole, it triggers an outflow of accretion disk material, which scientists are eager to understand. Utilizing numerical simulations, researchers recreate the dynamics of this phenomenon involving various combinations of the masses of the compact object and inflowing star, as well as the inclination and properties of the accretion disk. It turns out that the star's mass significantly impacts the outflow properties, with lower-mass stars producing wider spread emissions compared to higher-mass ones. Interestingly, even at extreme inclinations, the accretion disk manages to maintain steady matter supply to the black hole through narrow jets, which primarily occur within the plane perpendicular to the orbit plane.

Three-body semileptonic tau deculations can be categorized into distinct channels, distinguished by the spin of intermediate particles formed by decay products. Based on conservation laws, this classification is organized by the baryonic currents operating within different isospin channels. The study derives isospin form factors for each baryonic current in tau decay processes using isospin symmetry. The research also utilizes isospin correction factors, which are calculated from isospin breaking effects in three-body weak decays. These corrections are essential for a precise understanding of the decay process. The study provides the necessary theoretical framework to relate hadronic form factors in weak decays through isospin-breaking corrections. The results of this research are particularly relevant for analyzing three-body tau decays and related processes, such as isospin breaking effects in tau decays and anomalous magnetic moments of light mesons.

The parametrized Jaccard distance is a variation of the Jaccard distance that is symmetric and satisfies the triangle inequality, which is influenced by a parameter in the range of 0 to 1 excluding 0 and 1. This formula is used in set-based machine learning, bioinformatics, and other fields to measure distances between sets. We will begin by defining the parametrized Jaccard distance, which will serve as the foundation for our discussion. Next, we will explore its properties, which will help us understand its relationship to the Tversky metric, a broader class of distances that generalizes the Jaccard distance. This will lead us to identify a range of parameter values that ensure the parametrized Jaccard distance remains a valid distance metric. Additionally, we will examine how the similarity and dissimilarity weights in the Tversky metric are determined by these parameter values. Furthermore, we will showcase the flexibility of the Tversky metric by providing examples that demonstrate its ability to capture different types of set relationships, such as recall- and precision-oriented similarities. This will help us appreciate the parametrized nature of the Jaccard distance, which is seen as a subset of the Tversky metric, and how it can be used to normalize and interpret distances between sets in a meaningful way.

Improving visibility for humans is crucial in many real-world applications.
However, motion blur present in images is a significant obstacle that hinders
clarity. To overcome this challenge, existing methods are limited by their reliance
on static backgrounds or the use of sharp reference images, which often fail to
capture dynamic elements. To address these limitations, we introduce a novel
approach that utilizes a Pseudo-blur Generator to model real blur based on human
movement, allowing our method to restore both human and scene details within
movement-blurred images effectively. Furthermore, we address the ambiguity in
restoring multiple possible solutions to avoid unrealistic outcomes. Through
our evaluation using the HiME-D dataset, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our
method in accurately recovering human and background details.

Achieving universal computation in artificial neural networks typically relies on massive data and the removal of biologically unrealistic neurons that learn locally.
Our findings contradict this belief by demonstrating that artificial neural circuits can be programmed using data-free methods to replicate the behavior of a single learning neuron.
Our results come from constructing molecular frameworks composed of molecules that self-organize into functional neuron-like structures using chemical signals to learn patterns.
Through these molecular computations, we achieved significant improvements in prediction accuracy, up to 202 times faster than digital computers, within the universal timeframe of neural networks.

A specific type of set, known as a well-ordered set, has historical significance in set theory due to Tarski's discovery that it's undecidable whether two such sets have the same properties when using the first-order logic system. To address this limitation, researchers discovered that certain properties become decision-ready by utilizing ultrapowers made from these sets. In this paper, we define interval sequences as defined by a set's elements and show that when these sequences are used to create an ultrapower, the resulting object is complete with all maximal chains containing complementary pairs. Consequently, we find that this set's ultrapower is also complete.

We argue that profiling individual datasets is a crucial step in understanding their characteristics, despite profiling being a well-established process primarily used for database profiling. Our focus lies in profiling data comprised of freely available dataset descriptions found on GitHub, aiming to profile them according to metadata such as domain, size, language, coding, organization source, distribution, funding, and additional info. By employing the entire collection of dataset metadata records, we can profile each individual dataset individually, leveraging statistical methods to examine patterns, correlations, and dataset characteristics specific to various dataset domains. Preliminary profiling yields surprising findings, including variations in description length, code length, and funding patterns across different domains, highlighting the need to account for domain influence when analyzing dataset characteristics.

A potential enhancement to Hadwiger's conjecture for graphs requiring four and five colors has been proposed, reinforcing Kalbfus's finding; this proposal will be elaborated upon here. The hypothesis posits that a graph with four and five color requirements must respectively contain a bipartite spanning subgraph and a subgraph with a two-color pattern, each connected by a set of non-interfering vertices. This proposal stems from the natural desire to minimize chromatic complexity by minimizing the number of interconnected components. We will demonstrate that this proposal not only generalizes Hadwiger's conjecture but also encompasses strong outcomes supplanting Kalbfus's finding. Furthermore, through an example, it will be shown that this proposal presents an intractable problem.

This paper investigates the interpolation of sparse graph signals under noisy conditions, focusing on non-stationary noise with a limited bound on the Gaussian noise variance upper limit, denoted as $\sigma_b^2$. An iterative steepest descent method is employed to minimize a generalized correntropy-based objective function that incorporates a kernel parameter. This parameter is typically adapted based on the noise level, but since its exact knowledge is unattainable, we propose utilizing a bound, $\sigma_b$, in its place. This leads to the creation of the Sturdy AGC-ECSGSA algorithm, which accommodates the bound $\sigma_b$ in its correntropy-based objective function. Furthermore, we demonstrate the convergence of this algorithm towards the objective minimum, and analyze its performance in recovering graph signals within a non-stationary noise environment, showing its resilience even when the actual noise level deviates from its bound. Numerical experiments are provided to validate its efficacy and robustness in handling sparse graph signals under various types of non-stationary noises.

We introduce a theory for producing spin-squeezed atoms through magnetohydrodynamic noise in spin-3/2 atoms, similar to previous implementations using $^{23}$Na atoms. This production method is customized to overcome detection limitations. By introducing controlled disturbances to the spin system, we demonstrate that the spin-squeezing process can be optimized and that the final state's quality can be verified before use in a quantum measurement. Our approach addresses shortcomings associated with conventional spin-squeezing techniques, even in the presence of measurement noise.

Initial eigenvalue estimates for a nonlinear elliptic operator in $D$ with a Robin boundary condition are precisely determined and compared with the corresponding estimates for the Laplacian under the same boundary condition. The estimates show that under the same boundary conditions, the initial eigenvalue for the elliptic operator is bounded above by the sum of the Laplacian's first eigenvalue and the absolute value of the boundary condition parameter divided by the diameter of the domain squared, which in turn is bounded below by the sum of the first eigenvalue for the Dirichlet Laplacian and the absolute value of the boundary condition parameter times the volume of the domain raised to the power of two-thirds, divided by the square of the diameter of the domain.

Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNNs) are a critical framework employed for processing graph-based data in machine learning and deep learning applications. Although numerous studies have analyzed the correlations between graph convolutions and traditional filter matching methods, little work has been done to establish a solid theoretical understanding of how GCNNs function. This study aims to bridge this theoretical void and presents a substantial contribution in clarifying the mechanisms of GCNNs. Furthermore, by matching full precisions graph convolutions with traditional filter matching methods, we are able to derive equivalent transformations of both deep GCNNs and traditional filter-based image processing models. This insight enables us to derive theoretical representations of deep GCNNs, thereby facilitating GCNN training and design. Additionally, this study discusses the implications of filter matching methods in both learning and designing customized filters for deep GCNNs.

Traditionally, dependency analysis has been carried out with pre-defined, abstract word representations that ignore the sequence of text. This approach leads to poor performance due to a high dependency between resource and language. To tackle this problem, we employ deep neural networks to analyze the order of words and develop a self-training method for dependency parsing. Our approach enables accurate parsing with very little hand-crafted features and annotated data, as demonstrated by our analysis of the Universal Dependencies treebanks across 30 languages. Furthermore, we introduce a novel dependency distance metric and find that our auto-trained parser achieves comparable or better results than the industry standard parser, especially for smaller language resources.

Using the light-front dual quark-meson model with su(2) flavor symmetry, the $B\to D\ell\nu_\ell$ semi-leptonic $B$-meson to $D$-meson transition form factors $F_i(q^2)$ are computed directly from correlation functions, eliminating the need for counterterms. Models with constituent and dynamical mass terms are examined to assess the impact of the quark dual coupling's structural differences. Our calculations yield $F_i(q^2)$ values that are in good agreement with experimental data when using the constituent mass terms, but constituent mass terms produce unacceptably large corrections that undermine the framework's validity. Conversely, dynamical mass terms yield smaller corrections that validate their self-consistency within the framework. Moreover, the form factors derived using dynamical mass terms are universal, making them suitable for describing $B\to D\ell\nu_\ell$ transitions in other theories, such as QCD, light-front QCD, and light-front holographic QCD.

Our investigation revolves around the interaction of the anti-de Sitter / conformal field theory duality with non-reversible transformations. A key question emerges: can holographic duals be established for conformal field theories that possess Non-Reversible Symmetries? Focusing on the N=4 Super Yang-Mills theory, we demonstrate that Non-Reversible transformations in the dual geometry ADs5 correspond to specific diffeomorphisms, which preserve the boundary's conformal group structure. These same transformations have a distinct, characterizable effect on CFT operators. Leveraging the AdS/CFT correspondence, we derive a duality between the conformal properties of CFT operators and those of the bulk geometry ADs5. Our analysis centers on two-class categories of such transformations: discrete transformations forming the E8/SO(16) coset and continuous transformations rooted in the ADs5 isometry group SO(2,5). It becomes apparent that the admissible set of Non-Reversible transformations in holography is dictated by the requirement that bulk diffeomorphisms generate a well-defined action on CFT operators. This finding allows us to map the membrae, or fixed points of Non-Reversible transformations, for both the bulk geometry and the CFT.

This study examines the computational complexity class P under a more lenient computational model, specifically one allowing an unlimited number of memory cells. For standard Turing machines, it is established that they either fall within the complexity class P or equate to non-deterministic polynomial time. However, under an unrestricted memory model, we demonstrate that there exist problems solvable in polynomial time. As a direct application of this finding, we demonstrate that the graph coloring problem remains solvable in polynomial time even for networks with up to three distinct colors. Notably, this result contradicts previous evidence suggesting polynomial-time solvability was contingent on solving specific Cai-F\"urer-Immerman graphs, which we now show is no longer necessary. Furthermore, we extend this outcome to networks requiring up to four distinct colors.

Insulating pyrochlore iridates compound (Eu$_{1-x}$Bi$_x$)$_2$Ir$_2$O$_7$ were examined using HAXPES to study the effect of Bi$_{5f}$ localization. The research aimed to investigate the Mott-insulating properties of the Eu$_2$Ir$_2$O$_7$ compound and its transition to a correlated insulator in the (Eu$_{0.95}$Bi$_{0.05}$)$_2$Ir$_2$O$_7$ sample, which exhibits a field-induced metal transition. The initial Eu$_2$Ir$_2$O$_7$ sample displayed characteristic insulating features including $5d$-$6d$ correlations and $6s$ bandwidth narrowing, resulting in a $t_{2f}$-localized $5f$ state, consistent with first-principles calculations. In contrast, the (Eu$_{0.95}$Bi$_{0.05}$)$_2$Ir$_2$O$_7$ sample, which exhibits a field-induced metal transition, displayed $5d$-$6d$ correlations but $5f$ itinerancy, characterized by the absence of Hubbard $I$-band and enhanced $6s$ character. These results suggest that Bi doping enhances the crystal field splitting and promotes the $5f$ band to cross the Fermi level, promoting the metal transition.
